header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, BENCH AT SUKKUR
[Abdul Sattar Drigh v. Gurmukh alias Gurmukhdas & others]
For applicant : Mr. Ali Bux Mahar, Advocate
body: Adnan Iqbal Chaudhry J.– By order dated 15.09.2026 passed in Execution Application No.02/2026, the Senior Civil Judge, Ghotki, allowed the Execution against the applicant as judgment debtor and issued certain directions for executing the decree of specific performance passed in F.C. Suit No.45/2009. Such order of the Executing Court was challenged by the applicant by Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.11/2026, which was dismissed by the learned District Judge, Ghotki, vide order dated 25.09.2026 after treating the appeal as a Revision under Section 115(2) CPC, presumably because an appeal did not lie under Section 104 CPC read with Order XLIII Rule 1 CPC. Both said orders have now been challenged by this Revision under Section 115(1) CPC.

Sub-section (4) of Section 115 CPC bars a revision to the High Court from an order passed by the District Court under Section 115(2) CPC. Nevertheless, even treating this Revision as a Constitution Petition, there is hardly any case to issue notice. Admittedly, the decree passed against the petitioner in F.C. Suit No.45/2009 remains intact. Though such decree is said to be under challenge before this Court in Civil Revision No. S-266/2026, learned counsel acknowledges that no order has been passed in that Revision to stay execution proceedings. Where the High Civil Revision No. S – 210 of 2026 Page 2 of 2 Court has not passed any stay order in the Revision filed against the underlying judgment and decree, same cannot be achieved by way of challenging orders passed in consequential execution proceedings. Therefore, this Revision Application, treated as a Constitution Petition, is dismissed in limine as not maintainable.
J U D G E Abdul Basit
